arxiv-2208-04074.title: Bug-Fix Variants: Visualizing Unique Source Code Changes across GitHub Forks
arxiv-2208-04074.creator: Daigo Imamura, Takashi Ishio, Raula Gaikovina Kula, Kenichi Matsumoto
arxiv-2208-04074.description: Abstract Forking is a common practice for developers when building upon on already existing projects. These forks create variants, which have a common code base but then evolve the code in different directions, which is specific to that forked project requirements.

arxiv-2208-05222.title: Alfvénic waves in the inhomogeneous solar atmosphere
arxiv-2208-05222.creator: R. J. Morton, R. Sharma, E. Tajfirouze, H. Miriyala
arxiv-2208-05222.description: Abstract The solar atmosphere is known to be replete with magneto-hydrodynamic wave modes, and there has been significant investment in understanding how these waves propagate through the Sun’s atmopshere and deposit their energy into the plasma. The waves’ journey is made interesting by the vertical variation in plasma quantities that define the solar atmosphere.

arxiv-2210-08464.title: Federated Learning with Privacy-Preserving Ensemble Attention Distillation Thanks: X. Gong, L. Song, R. Vedula, J. Yuan and D. Doermann are with University at Buffalo, Buffalo NY, USA ({xuangong, lsong8, rishisat, jsyuan, doermann}@buffalo.edu). A. Sharma, M. Zheng, B. Planche, A Innanje, T. Chen an
arxiv-2210-08464.creator: Xuan Gong, Liangchen Song, Rishi Vedula, Abhishek Sharma, Meng Zheng, Benjamin Planche
arxiv-2210-08464.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where many local nodes collaboratively train a central model while keeping the training data decentralized. This is particularly relevant for clinical applications since patient data are usually not allowed to be transferred out of medical facilities, leading to the need for FL.

arxiv-2310-13388.title: Music Augmentation and Denoising for Peak-Based Audio Fingerprinting
arxiv-2310-13388.description: Abstract Audio fingerprinting is a well-established solution for song identification from short recording excerpts. Popular methods rely on the extraction of sparse representations, generally spectral peaks, and have proven to be accurate, fast, and scalable to large collections. However, real-world applications of audio identification often happen in noisy environments, which can cause these systems to fail.

arxiv-2402-08210.title: Quantum Computing-Enhanced Algorithm Unveils Novel Inhibitors for KRAS
arxiv-2402-08210.creator: Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Christoph Gorgulla, AkshatKumar Nigam, Dmitry Bezrukov, Daniel Varoli, Alex Aliper, Daniil Polykovsky, Krishna M. Padmanabha Das, Jamie Snider, Anna Lyakisheva, Ardalan Hosseini Mansob, Zhong Yao, Lela Bitar, Eugene Radchenko, Xiao Ding, Jinxin Liu, Fanye Meng, Feng Ren, Yudon
arxiv-2402-08210.description: Abstract Abstract The discovery of small molecules with therapeutic potential is a long-standing challenge in chemistry and biology. Researchers have increasingly leveraged novel computational techniques to streamline the drug development process to increase hit rates and reduce the costs associated with bringing a drug to market.

arxiv-2402-12877.title: Görtler number-based scaling of boundary-layer transition on rotating cones in axial inflow
arxiv-2402-12877.creator: Sumit Tambe 1 2, Kentaro Kato 3, Zahir Hussain 4
arxiv-2402-12877.description: Abstract This paper reports on the efficacy of the Görtler number in scaling the laminar-turbulent boundary-layer transition on rotating cones facing axial inflow. Depending on the half-cone angle ψ \psi and axial flow strength, the competing centrifugal and crossflow instabilities dominate the transition.

arxiv-2407-15378.title: Experimental study on the relationship between extensional and shear rheology of low-viscosity power-law fluids
arxiv-2407-15378.creator: Yuzuki Matsumoto, Misa Kawaguchi, Yoshiyuki Tagawa
arxiv-2407-15378.description: Abstract This paper investigates the relationship between extensional and shear viscosity of low-viscosity power-law fluids. We show the first experimental evidence of the conditions satisfying the same power exponents for extensional and shear viscosity, as indicated by the Carreau model.

arxiv-2501-12660.title: Extracting General-use Transformers for Low-resource Languages via Knowledge Distillation
arxiv-2501-12660.creator: Jan Christian Blaise Cruz and Alham Fikri Aji
arxiv-2501-12660.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jan Christian Blaise Cruz and Alham Fikri Aji. In this paper, we propose the use of simple knowledge distillation to produce smaller and more efficient single-language transformers from Massively Multilingual Transformers (MMTs) to alleviate tradeoffs associated with the use of such in low-resource settings. Using Tagalog as a case study, we show that these smaller single-language models perform on-par with strong baselines in a variety of benchmark tasks in a much more efficient manner.

arxiv-2504-01056.description: Abstract This is a review of Frank Lad’s book “Just Plain Wrong: The Dalliance of Quantum Theory with the Defiance of Bell’s Inequality” (Austin Macauley Publishers, 2024). In the Preface of his book, Frank Lad writes ( Lad2024 , p.

arxiv-2509-07110.title: Indirect detection of boosted light scalar dark matter
arxiv-2509-07110.creator: Arindam Basu
arxiv-2509-07110.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arindam Basu. We explore the possibilities of detecting MeV-scale boosted dark matter (DM) via astrophysical observations. Given a particular model framework, using gamma-ray data from COMPTEL and EGRET , as well as neutrino constraints from the Super-Kamiokande , Hyper-Kamiokande , JUNO , diffuse supernova neutrino background ( DSNB ), and atmospheric neutrino observations, we find that boosted light scalar DM could be probed within the mass range of ∼ − 80 \sim 20\!-\!80 MeV, satisfying the Planck observed relic abundance.

arxiv-2510-20227.title: Optimization of Bregman–Variational Learning Dynamics
arxiv-2510-20227.creator: Jinho Cha, Youngchul Kim, Jungmin Shin, Jaeyoung Cho, Seon Jin Kim, Junyeol Ryu, [6pt] Department of Computer Science, Gwinnett Technical College, Lawrenceville, GA, USA, [4pt] Corresponding author: jinho.cha@gwinnetttech.edu
arxiv-2510-20227.description: Abstract We develop a general optimization-theoretic framework for Bregman–Variational Learning Dynamics (BVLD), a new class of operator-based updates that unify Bayesian inference, mirror descent, and proximal learning under time-varying environments. Each update is formulated as a variational optimization problem combining a smooth convex loss f t f_{t} with a Bregman divergence D ψ D_{\psi} .

arxiv-2602-16211.description: Abstract We study a model of auction design where a seller is selling a set of objects to a set of agents who can be assigned no more than one object. Each agent’s preference over (object, payment) pair need not be quasilinear.

Numerous features distinguish prokaryotes from eukaryotes, chief among which are the distinctive internal membrane systems of eukaryotic cells. pmc-11416917.title: Traumatic Floating Clavicle: A Case Report and Updated Literature Review
pmc-11416917.creator: Chittawee Jiamton, Pariwat Taweekitikul, Techit Leelasestaporn, Pongsakorn Rungchamrussopa, Thongchai Laohathaimongkol
pmc-11416917.description: Traumatic floating clavicle or bipolar dislocation is a rare injury. Herein, we present a case of ipsilateral sternoclavicular and acromioclavicular joint dislocation after a motorcycle accident. The patient was a 43-year-old man who presented with right shoulder pain and limited range of motion.

pmc-11531467.title: Predicting removal of arsenic from groundwater by iron based filters using deep neural network models
pmc-11531467.creator: Muhammad Ali Martuza, Md Shafiquzzaman, Husnain Haider, Amimul Ahsan, Abdelkader T Ahmed
pmc-11531467.description: Arsenic (As) contamination in drinking water has been highlighted for its environmental significance and potential health implications. Iron-based filters are cost-effective and sustainable solutions for As removal from contaminated water. Applying Machine Learning (ML) models to investigate and optimize As removal using iron-based filters is limited.

pmc-11585598.title: Isolating Cu-Zn active-sites in Ordered Intermetallics to Enhance Nitrite-to-Ammonia Electroreduction
pmc-11585598.creator: Jiao Lan, Zhen Wang, Cheng-wei Kao, Ying-Rui Lu, Feng Xie, Yongwen Tan
pmc-11585598.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Electrocatalytic nitrite reduction to the valuable ammonia is a green and sustainable alternative to the conventional Haber-Bosch method for ammonia synthesis, while the activity and selectivity for ammonia production remains poor at low nitrite concentrations.

pmc-12469884.title: Table Tennis for Health: A Multidimensional Perspective on Its Physical, Emotional, and Social Advantages
pmc-12469884.creator: Pilar Aparicio-Chueca, Noa Muñoz-Vila, José Arturo Abraldes, Adrián Mateo-Orcajada, Raquel Vaquero-Cristobal
pmc-12469884.description: Background/Objectives: Table tennis is commonly perceived as a recreational or competitive sport; however, growing evidence highlights its potential as a multidimensional tool for health promotion. This study investigates the perceived physical, cognitive, emotional, and social benefits of regular table tennis practice, emphasizing its contribution to health beyond the purely sporting dimension.

pmc-12484360.title: (Not) just policy success: Incorporating justice in policy evaluation
pmc-12484360.creator: Nynke van Uffelen, Nihit Goyal, Amanda Martinez-Reyes
pmc-12484360.description: Despite the recognition that policy evaluations are inherently normative as they are shaped by political and social values, justice is rarely addressed systematically in policy evaluation practice or research. By overlooking structural inequities and failing to scrutinize power dynamics, this omission risks hindering accountability, legitimizing injustice, and inhibiting policy learning.

pmc-12633980.title: Identifying knowledge gap and adherence barriers for diabetic retinopathy screening: Findings from primary healthcare clinics in Pakistan
pmc-12633980.creator: Asra Qureshi, Maham Fatima, Shirin Jalaluddin, Karim Damji, Haroon Tayyab, Unab I. Khan
pmc-12633980.description: Context:Diabetes is a leading cause of mortality globally, with a growing prevalence in low- and middle-income countries. The increasing burden of diabetes has led to a surge in diabetic retinopathy (DR), a major cause of preventable blindness, emphasizing the need to address poor screening practices.

pmc-12732643.title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Recombinant Tumor Necrosis Factor Receptor: Fc Fusion Protein as First-Line Treatment for Active Rheumatoid Arthritis in China
pmc-12732643.creator: Rui Zhang, Aixia Ma
pmc-12732643.description: Highlights What are the main findings? rhTNFR:Fc provided 0.74 additional QALYs at an incremental cost of CNY 9447.96 versus methotrexate, giving an ICER of CNY 12,783.56 per QALY, well below the 2024 China per capita GDP threshold. Results were robust in probabilistic analysis and most sensitive to utility inputs; adverse events were broadly similar across arms.

pmc-12757714.title: Identifying Time-Variant Predictors of Interest in Completing Brief Digital Mental Health Interventions Among Adult Survivors of Cancer: Ecological Momentary Assessment Study
pmc-12757714.creator: Katharine E Daniel, James W Kinchen, Angela Chang, Patrick H Finan, Philip I Chow
pmc-12757714.description: BackgroundDigital microinterventions have strong potential to improve the lives of adults diagnosed with cancer. However, little is known about which types of digital microinterventions are most desired and how contextual factors may influence those preferences. This potentially limits guidance for personalized and timely digital microintervention delivery.

pmc-13024363.title: Thyroid Hormone Indices and Histopathological Severity of Diabetic Nephropathy in Euthyroid Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Biopsy-Based Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13024363.creator: Xiaorong Wang, Congqin Zhang, Xue Zhao, Sinan Zhao, Fang Zhang, Chunhui Li, Yongmei Hao
pmc-13024363.description: PurposeThyroid hormones (THs) influence glucose homeostasis, vascular tone, and renal hemodynamics. Whether subtle variations in TH indices within the euthyroid range are associated with histopathological severity of diabetic nephropathy (DN) is unclear. We examined the association between TH indices and renal pathological severity in euthyroid patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and biopsy-proven DN.

pmc-13062079.title: An explainable GeoAI framework for spatial assessment of wildfire susceptibility in the Upper Ravi sub-basin, Indian Himalaya
pmc-13062079.creator: Suheb, Md Nawazuzzoha, Md Shahid Ali, Md. Mamoon Rashid, Darakhsha Fatma Naqvi, Honey Qaisar, Pierre Sicard, Shankar Karuppannan, Hasan Raja Naqvi
pmc-13062079.description: Wildfires have emerged as a significant environmental concern in the Himalayan region, particularly in the Upper Ravi sub-basin of Himachal Pradesh, India. This study aims to map wildfire susceptibility by integrating Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing data, and advanced ensemble machine learning techniques.

pmc-13495301.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of fatty acid composition in polycystic ovary syndrome: perspectives from blood and follicular fluid

pmc-13557506.title: Prospects of HIV elimination among men who have sex with men: A systematic review of modeling studies
pmc-13557506.creator: Jacob Aiden Roberts, Alexandra Teslya, Mirjam E. Kretzschmar, Janneke H.H.M. van de Wijgert, Ganna Rozhnova
pmc-13557506.description: Men who have sex with men (MSM) remain disproportionately affected by HIV worldwide. This systematic review summarizes the results of mathematical modeling studies that evaluated prospects of HIV elimination among MSM by geographical setting, type of intervention(s), elimination definition, and model characteristics.

pmc-13599311.title: A comprehensive proteome and the first phosphoproteome reveal extensive phosphorylation of carbohydrate metabolism in Cryptosporidium parvum sporozoites
pmc-13599311.creator: Dongqiang Wang, Meng Li, Chenchen Wang, Haitao Li, Jigang Yin, Guan Zhu
pmc-13599311.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCryptosporidium parvum is an obligate apicomplexan parasite and a major cause of diarrheal disease in humans and animals worldwide. Despite its public health importance, the molecular regulation of parasite metabolism, particularly at the post-translational level, remains poorly understood. This study aims to understand major pathways regulated by protein phosphorylation in sporozoites, the parasite invasive stage, by comparative analysis of the proteomic and phosphoproteomic profiles.MethodsThe proteome and phosphoproteome of excysted sporozoites of C. parvum were determined by data-independent acquisition-based mass spectrometry.
